items.q: What is Lokmangal Multistate Co-operative Society Ltd.?
items.a: Lokmangal Multistate is a multi-state co-operative society registered under the Multi-State Co-operative Societies Act, 2002 (Registration No. MSCS/CR.216/2004). It follows the Act strictly and carries out financial business among its members.

items.q: How does the society use the deposits it receives?
items.a: Funds are lent to members and invested as permitted by the Co-operative Societies Act, its rules and the society’s bye-laws. Most of our lending is in the form of small business loans and micro-finance.

items.q: Are my deposits safe and secure?
items.a:
Yes. The Government of India has framed laws to protect deposits in multi-state co-operative societies, and Lokmangal follows every rule set by the Central Government. For example:

  • Rule 66 restricts a society (other than a co-operative bank) from lending to a member against the security of their own shares or of a non-member.
  • Rule 67 limits the deposits and loans a society may raise in a financial year to ten times its subscribed share capital and accumulated reserves (after deducting accumulated losses).

The wider Lokmangal Group’s turnover of over ₹1,000 crore is a further sign of the strength behind your deposits.

items.q: How is the society different from a finance company?
items.a:
A co-operative society is not owned by an individual. It is a democratic organisation run by a Board of Directors elected by members at the Annual General Meeting, and decisions are taken collectively and transparently. The Department of Co-operation reviews the society’s functioning regularly, and its accounts are statutorily audited and submitted to the Government of India every year.

When you invest with Lokmangal you are not just a depositor. You become a member and shareholder of the Lokmangal Parivar.

items.q: Why does Lokmangal pay a higher rate of interest?
items.a: We believe in encouraging the habit of saving among our members. Higher savings lead to higher investment and a stronger economy, so we share more of our earnings with the people who make them possible.

items.q: How can the society offer better rates than commercial banks?
items.a:
• Tax efficiency: interest earned on loans to members is exempt under Section 80P of the Income Tax Act, and the board passes part of this saving on to members.
  • No CRR or SLR: banks must park a portion of deposits as cash with the RBI and in low-yield securities. The society is exempt from both, so more of every rupee is put to productive use.
  • Secured lending: our short- and medium-term loans to members are fully secured, keeping recoveries strong.
  • Low operating costs: lean operations compared to banks and NBFCs mean more value returned to members.
Anyone looking for better returns on short-, medium- or long-term deposits is welcome. Visit any of our branches or contact us to get started.

items.q: Is TDS deducted on my interest?
items.a: TDS is applicable on interest earned on deposits, except for members of the society. If you do not have a PAN, submit Form 60/61 when opening your deposit.

items.q: Do senior citizens get a higher rate?
items.a: Yes. On Vishwamangal Fixed Deposits of up to 364 days, senior citizens, persons with disabilities, ex-servicemen, single parents, widows aged 50 and above, and bulk deposits of ₹25 lakh & above receive an additional 0.50% p.a. See the full interest rate chart.
